expected: Generate/queue cancellation and transport loss; next turn valid; no false completion or duplicate side effects.
limitations: OMP itself never queues its own requests (maxInFlightRequests 1); the queued-client case needs a second concurrent client.
observed: Client loss while generating: the server stops within 64 ms (finish disconnect) and the next turn is valid. A completed side effect followed by client loss is not repeated on resume (1 execution, 1 log line). A failed tool is followed by a valid turn. Queue cancellation: a client that disconnects while queued behind a generating request no longer harms later requests: the generating request continued, the server went idle 269 ms after it was dropped, and 5/5 follow-up requests were served correctly with no engine restart. The minimal g14q probe, which reproduced the v0.1.27 defect 2/2 (HTTP 400 'cancelled' then an engine exit), now passes on v0.1.30: in both queued-disconnect scenarios and the control, two consecutive 8,123-token prompts returned 200 with the same engine process (Strata#183, fixed in v0.1.28).
